column1: # Exact pinned client-go test evidence for Campaign 16 BatchCommands wire and in-flight core.

column8: One published ID receives exactly one terminal completion through its route generation; real BatchCommands duplex streaming and live TiKV remain external.
Cancellation retires the pending entry and suppresses late publication; production timer scheduling and a live timed-out stream remain external.
Route-scoped failure drains owned entries once with structured transport facts; a real callback closing the client and tonic stream shutdown remain external.
A closed route fails before pending publication and cannot double-complete; real client close and transport scheduling remain external.
Opaque immutable bodies preserve exact encoded bytes and pinned oneof tags; concrete protobuf command encoding and allocator parity remain external.
Supported command tags and immutable encoded ownership are translated; the complete client-go request switch remains external.
Owned bytes eliminate shared pool lifetime edge cases and remain stable across commands; Go pool reuse and allocator behavior are intentionally not reproduced.
Immutable owned bytes remain valid without a return-to-pool state; concrete protobuf body parity remains external.
Request bytes have one owner and require no reuse bookkeeping; Go pool capacity reuse is eliminated rather than emulated.
Rust ownership makes double return unrepresentable; allocator and pool accounting parity remain outside the semantic port.
Immutable per-entry bytes remove shared pool concurrency from the runtime; Go race-detector and allocation-pool performance parity remain external.
The sole in-flight table exposes deterministic pending IDs by route generation and rejects duplicates; production inspection hooks and live stream state remain external.
Pinned response tags demultiplex to the exact opaque command kind and reject missing or mismatched envelopes; concrete response protobuf decoding remains external.
The pinned oneof layout and unknown-command rejection preserve the regression boundary; the complete generated client-go command universe remains external.
